mainTopic: The limits on comparing a נדה's blood to her, the sources and limits of טומאה from a dead body's parts, and the source that זוב is טמא
overview: The גמרא first asks whether a נדה's blood shares her special power of אבן מסמא. רב אשי answers that the word ״אותם״ limits that rule. Next, ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן give two different פסוקים for why dry בשר המת is טמא. Their sources lead to different rulings about flesh that has crumbled. A משנה says the teeth, hair and nails of a מת are טהור, and רב אדא בר אהבה explains this with a two-part test: only parts that were created with the person and do not grow back are like a bone. The גמרא tests his rule against skin, using עולא's statement about a rabbinic גזרה, and against flesh, which leaves a scar. Finally, a ברייתא learns from ״זובו טמא״ that זוב is טמא, since a קל וחומר fails because of the שעיר המשתלח. רב ביבי בר אביי begins to explain why the פסוק must be teaching more than טומאה by touching, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Should her blood also make things impure under a heavy stone?
steps.stepSummary: If the blood of a נדה is compared to the נדה herself, maybe the blood should also carry her special power of אבן מסמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as she makes things impure through a heavy stone, her menstrual flow should also make things impure through a heavy stone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison made earlier between a נדה and her blood. It says that if they are equal, the blood should share every one of her impurity powers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב or נדה has a special power. If she sits on a very heavy stone, a vessel under the stone becomes טמא, even though her weight does not press on it. If her blood is treated just like her, the blood should have this power too, and that sounds wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A very heavy stone; a vessel under it becomes טמא when a זב or נדה sits on the stone
Her menstrual flow (her blood)
"If so, just as... so too...": pushing a comparison to an unwanted result

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about touching or carrying. The vessel under the stone feels no pressure from her at all, and that is exactly why the rule is so unusual.

phrases.english: If so, just as she transmits impurity
phrases.notes: "She" is the נדה herself. The earlier comparison treated her blood like her.

phrases.english: through a very heavy stone,
so too her menstrual flow should also transmit impurity
through a very heavy stone?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה הִיא מְטַמְּאָה בְּאֶבֶן מְסָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of a נדה's blood to the נדה herself from the earlier part of the sugya
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison that makes the blood of a נדה equal to the נדה herself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full comparison would give the blood her special אבן מסמא power, which seems unacceptable

steps.title: The word 'them' limits the heavy-stone rule
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the word ״אותם״ in the פסוק is a מיעוט that keeps the blood out of the אבן מסמא rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The verse says "and he that carries them." The word "them" is a limitation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. He shows from a word in the פסוק that the heavy-stone rule does not reach the blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about things under a זב says "and he that carries them." The word "them" narrows the rule to those items, such as משכב ומושב. So the general comparison between the blood and the נדה still stands, but this one special power is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: A limitation; a word in the פסוק that narrows a rule
Items made for lying or sitting, which have special impurity rules

steps.whatToRemember: The blood is compared to the נדה in general, but ״אותם״ keeps it out of the special אבן מסמא rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The verse states: "And he that carries them"
"Them" is a limitation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אָמַר קְרָא ״וְהַנּוֹשֵׂא אוֹתָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting word in the פסוק (מיעוט) that carves out an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A full comparison would give the blood every power of the נדה, including אבן מסמא
steps.terutzMaskana: ״אותם״ limits the אבן מסמא rule, so the blood does not make things טמא through a heavy stone

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule for a corpse's flesh?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's next case and asks for the source that בשר המת is טמא whether moist or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the flesh of a corpse, from where do we derive it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, which says בשר המת is טמא both moist and dry. It asks for the source, setting up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new section. The question is specifically about dry flesh: we might have thought that once it dries out, it no longer counts as part of the dead body.

keyTerms.meaning: The flesh of a dead person
From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And the flesh of a corpse, from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that בשר המת is טמא even when dry

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns it from 'any of his impurity'
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש learns from ״לכל טומאתו״ that everything that comes off a dead body is טמא, moist or dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: The verse says "from any impurity that he has," meaning all impurities that come off of him.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the first source. The word "any" in the פסוק widens the rule to include every kind of impurity that comes from a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Any" works as a widening word (ריבוי). It brings in everything that separates from the dead body, without any difference between moist and dry. So dry flesh is still טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: "From any impurity that he has": the words being explained
Impurities that separate (come off) from the body
A widening; a word that adds more cases to a rule

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
The verse states: "from any impurity that he has"
meaning all impurities that come off of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אָמַר קְרָא ״לְכֹל טֻמְאָתוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לכל טומאתו״ includes every impurity that comes off the dead body, moist or dry

steps.title: רבי יוחנן compares the dead body to a bone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns it from "the bone of a man": the dead body is like a bone, and a bone is dry, so dry flesh is also טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: "Or the bone of a man, or a grave." A man is compared to a bone: just as a bone is dry, so too here, even dry.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different source. He reads the פסוק as putting "man" side by side with "bone," so the dead body follows the rules of a bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bone is dry, and it is still טמא. Since the פסוק links the dead body to a bone, dry flesh stays טמא as well. This is a comparison (דומיא), unlike ריש לקיש's widening word.

keyTerms.meaning: A human bone
Similar to; comparable to
Dry

steps.whatToRemember: Both sages agree that dry בשר המת is טמא. They only disagree about the source: ריש לקיש uses the word "any" (ריבוי), and רבי יוחנן uses the bone comparison.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
"Or the bone of a man, or a grave"
a man is similar to a bone:
just as a bone is dry,
so too here, even when dry.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: ״אוֹ בְעֶצֶם אָדָם אוֹ בְקָבֶר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different source for the same rule given by ריש לקיש in step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dead body is compared to a bone; just as a bone is dry and טמא, dry flesh is also טמא

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between ריש לקיש's source and רבי יוחנן's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: Both ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן agree that dry flesh of a מת is טמא, so the גמרא asks if their different sources ever lead to a different law. This question sets up the answer in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two sages give different פסוקים for the same rule, the גמרא often asks whether the difference matters in practice. Here ריש לקיש used "לכל טומאתו" (everything from the body) and רבי יוחנן used "עצם אדם" (like a bone). The גמרא wants a case where these two readings would give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? A standard question asking for the practical difference between two opinions.

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two sources just given.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where ריש לקיש's source and רבי יוחנן's source would give different rulings.

steps.title: The difference is flesh that has crumbled
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is flesh of a מת that is so dry it crumbles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is a case where the flesh has crumbled into crumbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sages differ about flesh that is so dry it falls apart into crumbs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, "לכל טומאתו" includes everything that comes from the body, so crumbled flesh is still טמא. For רבי יוחנן, the flesh must be like a bone, and a bone does not crumble, so crumbled flesh is טהור. The two sources agree on dry flesh but split on crumbled flesh.

keyTerms.meaning: Crumbled into crumbs; fell apart into small pieces
There is a difference between them

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where it crumbled into crumbs.
phrases.notes: For ריש לקיש this flesh is still טמא; for רבי יוחנן it is טהור, since a bone does not crumble.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Crumbled flesh: טמא according to ריש לקיש, טהור according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the exact פסוק a sage uses can change the law in a borderline case.

steps.title: A ברייתא says crumbled flesh is טהור
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that crumbled flesh of a מת is טהור, which seems to go against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: flesh of a מת that crumbled is טהור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge ריש לקיש. Step 7 explained that by his source, crumbled flesh would still be טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said that according to ריש לקיש, crumbled flesh is still טמא. This ברייתא says plainly that crumbled flesh is טהור. That fits רבי יוחנן but seems to go against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: That crumbled apart
Pure; not טמא

phrases.english: They raised an objection: flesh of a corpse that crumbled is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's side of the difference given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש, who holds that crumbled flesh is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules that crumbled flesh is טהור, against ריש לקיש's reading of "לכל טומאתו".

steps.title: The ברייתא means flesh that turned into dust
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about flesh that became like flour and is just dust.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is talking about flesh that became like flour and is now dust.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends ריש לקיש by saying the ברייתא means a different, more extreme case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not talking about flesh that broke into crumbs. It is talking about flesh that turned into powder like flour, which is just dust. Even ריש לקיש agrees that dust is טהור, so the ברייתא does not go against him.

keyTerms.meaning: There; in that source
That became like flour; turned into powder
Dust

phrases.english: There, it is where it became like flour
and it is dust.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case of the ברייתא to a more extreme situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls all crumbled flesh טהור, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only means flesh that turned to powder and is dust; crumbs are still טמא according to ריש לקיש.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases: "crumbled" (pieces) is the argument between the sages, while "like flour" (dust) is טהור according to everyone.

steps.title: A משנה says teeth, hair and nails of a מת are טהור
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that everything in a מת is טמא except teeth, hair and nails, which only count while attached.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: Everything in a מת makes things טמא, except the teeth, the hair and the nails. But while they are attached, everything is טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that says teeth, hair and nails of a מת are טהור once they come off. This challenges the sources given before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, "everything that comes from the body" is טמא, so teeth should be טמא. According to רבי יוחנן, things like a bone are טמא, and teeth are hard like bones. Yet the משנה says teeth that came off are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things טמא; passes on טומאה
Teeth
Hair
Fingernail or toenail
While they are attached to the body

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Everything that is in a corpse imparts impurity,
except for the teeth, the hair, and the nails;
but while they are attached, all is impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: כֹּל שֶׁבַּמֵּת מְטַמֵּא, חוּץ מִן הַשִּׁינַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge, this time against the sources themselves, not just against crumbled flesh.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sources of ריש לקיש ("everything from the body") and רבי יוחנן ("like a bone")
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Teeth come from the body and are hard like bone, yet the משנה says they are טהור once they come off.

steps.title: Only parts created with the person, like a bone
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that only parts that, like a bone, were there from birth are טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: It must be like a bone. Just as a bone was created with the person, so too only things that were created with him are טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה answers the challenge by explaining what "like a bone" means: a part that was there when the person was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bone is there from the time the person is born. So only parts that were there from birth are like a bone. Teeth grow in later, so they are not like a bone, and that is why the משנה calls them טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to a bone
That was created with him; there from birth

phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
It is similar to a bone:
phrases.notes: This goes back to the פסוק "עצם אדם" that רבי יוחנן used in step 5.

phrases.english: just as a bone is something that was created with him,
so too, everything that was created with him.
phrases.notes: Teeth are not there at birth; they grow in later, so they are left out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: דּוּמְיָא דְּעֶצֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the משנה in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the comparison to a bone more narrowly
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything hard and bone-like, such as teeth, should be טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only parts that were there from birth, like a bone, are טמא; teeth come later and are טהור.

steps.title: Hair and nails were there from birth, yet they are טהור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה: hair and nails were created with the person, yet the משנה calls them טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are hair and nails, which were created with him, and they are טהור!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's rule, because it does not explain the hair and nails in the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule explains the teeth, since they are not there at birth. But a baby is born with hair and nails. By his rule they should be טמא, yet the משנה says they are טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is; introduces a case that does not fit
They are pure

phrases.english: But there are hair and nails,
which were created with him, and they are pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאִיכָּא שֵׂעָר וְצִפּוֹרֶן, שֶׁנִּבְרְאוּ עִמּוֹ וּטְהוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule that whatever was created with the person is טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hair and nails are there from birth, so his rule would make them טמא, but the משנה says they are טהור.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה's revised rule: like a bone that never grows back
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה adds a second condition: a part is טמא only if it was created with the person AND does not grow back. This removes teeth, hair and nails from the rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא בר אהבה said: it must be similar to a bone. A bone was created with the person and does not grow back, so anything created with the person that does not grow back is טמא. Teeth are excluded because they were not created with him. Hair and nails are excluded because, even though they were created with him, they grow back.
steps.whatsHappening: Since step 12 showed that hair and nails were created with the person and still are not טמא, רב אדא בר אהבה fixes his rule by adding a second condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The model is still a bone, but now the comparison has two features: created with the person, and it does not regrow once removed. Teeth fail the first feature and hair and nails fail the second, so all three exceptions in the משנה are now explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Its root renews; if removed, it grows back
Are excluded (from the rule)

steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה's final rule has two tests: created with the person, and does not grow back. Teeth fail the first test, and hair and nails fail the second.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Similar to a bone:
just as a bone is something that was created with him
and its root does not renew,
phrases.notes: Literally "its stump does not replace": take it out and nothing new grows in its place.

phrases.english: so too, anything that was created with him
and whose root does not renew.
The teeth are excluded,
since they were not created with him;
hair and nails are excluded,
since even though they were created with him,
their root renews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rule that step 12 refuted by adding a second condition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refined criterion: adds the condition that the part does not regrow.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything created with the person is טמא, which would wrongly include hair and nails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only parts created with the person that do not grow back are טמא, like a bone.

steps.title: Challenge from skin, which grows back but is still treated as impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that skin grows back, since even חכמים agree about this in the case of a skinned animal. Yet a משנה lists human skin as being like flesh, meaning טמא. That contradicts רב אדא בר אהבה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about skin, which does grow back? We learned: an animal whose hide was removed, רבי מאיר says it is kosher and חכמים say it is unfit. Even חכמים only say unfit because in the meantime the air gets to it and it dies, but really the skin does grow back. And yet we learned: these are the ones whose skin counts like their flesh — human skin!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new rule. Skin grows back, so by רב אדא בר אהבה it should not be טמא, yet a משנה treats human skin like flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the גמרא proves from the case of the skinned animal that skin regrows. Even חכמים, who forbid the animal, agree that the skin itself comes back; the animal just dies from exposure first. Second, a different משנה counts human skin as equal to flesh for טומאה, which goes against the new rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hide was stripped off
Deems it kosher (fit to eat)
Deem it unfit
The air
Their skins have the same status as their flesh

phrases.english: But there is skin, whose root renews,
and we learned: an animal whose hide was removed:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in חולין about whether a skinned animal may still be eaten.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir deems it kosher, and the Sages deem it unfit.
And even the Rabbis do not deem it unfit
except because in the meantime
the air affects it and it dies,
but really, its root renews.
And we learned: these are the ones whose skin is like their flesh:
the skin of a person!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the new two-part rule against the case of skin.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule that things which grow back are not טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Skin grows back, as both sides agree about the skinned animal, yet a משנה treats human skin like flesh, which is טמא.

steps.title: עולא: human skin is impure only by rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: עולא already explained that by Torah law human skin is טהור. חז״ל made it טמא so that people would not use their parents' skins as rugs for a donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was already said about that משנה: עולא said that by Torah law human skin is pure. So why did they say it is impure? It is a decree, so that a person should not make the skins of his father and mother into rugs for a donkey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה about human skin does not hurt רב אדא בר אהבה, because that טומאה is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule is about Torah-level טומאה. On the Torah level, skin, which grows back, is טהור, just as his rule predicts. The משנה's ruling is an extra rabbinic decree meant to protect the dignity of the dead.

keyTerms.meaning: By Torah law (as opposed to rabbinic law)
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
Rugs or spreads

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a rabbinic stringency cannot be used to disprove a rule about Torah law.

phrases.english: It was already stated about it:
Ulla said: by Torah law
the skin of a person is pure,
so why did they say it is impure?
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים of the משנה that counted human skin like flesh.

phrases.english: It is a decree, lest a person make
the skins of his father and mother into rugs for a donkey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from human skin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Human skin is טמא from the Torah, which would contradict the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law, human skin is טהור. The טומאה is only a rabbinic safeguard, so the rule stands.

steps.title: Second version: skin does not grow back, yet עולא calls it pure
steps.stepSummary: In another version, the גמרא assumes that skin does NOT grow back. Then by רב אדא בר אהבה, human skin should be טמא from the Torah, yet עולא says it is טהור by Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way: what about skin, which does not grow back? We learned: and חכמים say it is unfit. Even רבי מאיר only says it is kosher because the flesh hardens and the animal heals, but really the skin does not grow back. And yet עולא said that by Torah law human skin is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the challenge with the facts about skin reversed. Now skin does not regrow, so it should be טמא, but עולא calls it טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even רבי מאיר agrees that the skin never comes back; the animal survives only because the flesh toughens over. That means skin fits the 'does not grow back' test and should be טמא from the Torah. עולא's ruling that it is טהור then becomes the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The flesh cools or hardens over
It heals and lives

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions reverse the facts. In the first, skin grows back and the problem is the משנה calling it טמא. In the second, skin does not grow back and the problem is עולא calling it טהור. עולא answers the first version but is the challenge in the second.

phrases.english: And some say:
But there is skin, whose root does not renew,
as we learned: and the Sages deem it unfit,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר לָא קָא מַכְשַׁר
phrases.english: and even Rabbi Meir does not deem it kosher
except because the flesh hardens and it heals,
but really, its root does not renew.
And yet Ulla said:
by Torah law the skin of a person is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הֲרֵי עוֹר, דְּאֵין גִּזְעוֹ מַחְלִיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the skin challenge in a second version with the opposite assumption about regrowth.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule that parts which do not grow back are טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Skin does not regrow, as even רבי מאיר admits, so it should be טמא from the Torah. Yet עולא rules that human skin is טהור by Torah law.

steps.title: עולא was only talking about tanned skin
steps.stepSummary: עולא's statement was said about the סיפא of the משנה, which deals with tanned skin. Untanned human skin stays טמא from the Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא's statement was about the end of the משנה: all these skins become טהור once tanned, except human skin. עולא said that by Torah law tanned human skin is טהור. חכמים made it טמא so that people would not turn their parents' skin into rugs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. It explains that עולא was only talking about skin that has been tanned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא never said that raw human skin is טהור from the Torah. He only said that tanned human skin is טהור. So raw human skin, which does not grow back, can be טמא from the Torah, just as רב אדא בר אהבה's rule says.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
He tanned them (processed the hide into leather)
Enough to count as tanning

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of skin. Raw human skin is טמא from the Torah. Tanned human skin is טמא only because of a גזרה of חכמים.

phrases.english: When Ulla's statement was said, it was said on the latter clause,
phrases.notes: He means the end part of the משנה that lists skins like flesh, the part about tanning.

phrases.english: "And all of them that one tanned
or that one walked on them as long as it takes to tan them
are pure, except for human skin."
And Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: דְּבַר תּוֹרָה עוֹר אָדָם כִּי עִבְּדּוֹ טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: By Torah law, human skin, when one tanned it, is pure.
And what is the reason they said it is impure?
It is a decree, lest a person make
the skin of his father and mother into rugs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by narrowing what עולא was talking about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: עולא's 'טהור by Torah law' applies only to tanned skin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought עולא said that all human skin is טהור from the Torah.
steps.terutzMaskana: Raw human skin is טמא from the Torah. Only tanned skin is טהור from the Torah, and its טומאה is a גזרה.

steps.title: Flesh grows back yet is impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אדא בר אהבה again: flesh heals and grows back, yet it is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But flesh grows back, and it is still טמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב אדא בר אהבה's 'does not grow back' condition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה said that only parts which do not grow back are טמא. When flesh is cut, it heals and fills back in, yet everyone agrees flesh is טמא. That seems to break his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh

phrases.english: But there is flesh,
whose root renews itself, and it is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the skin question is settled, a new challenge to the same rule from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's condition that only parts which do not grow back are טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flesh heals and grows back, yet it is טמא, so 'not growing back' cannot be the condition.

steps.title: Flesh leaves a scar, so it does not truly grow back
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי answers that healed flesh leaves a scar, so it is not a real regrowth.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר בר רב אשי said: when flesh is cut, a scar forms in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי answers the challenge about flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When flesh heals, it does not come back the way it was, because a scar is left behind. So flesh counts as something that does not grow back, and רב אדא בר אהבה's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A scar

steps.whatToRemember: רב אדא בר אהבה's rule: a body part is טמא only if it was created with the person and does not truly grow back. Flesh fits, because it leaves a scar.

phrases.english: Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Flesh: its place becomes a scar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי: בָּשָׂר נַעֲשֶׂה מְקוֹמוֹ צַלֶּקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: healing with a scar is not real regrowth.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flesh does not truly grow back, so it fits the rule.

steps.title: Where do we learn that זוב is impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'אבל הזוב' and asks for the source that זוב itself is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'But the זוב.' From where do we know that זוב is טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its Torah source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says זוב makes things טמא. The גמרא wants a Torah source showing that the discharge itself is a source of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discharge of a זב, a man with a certain bodily flow

phrases.english: "But the זוב."
Zov — from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion on another clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that זוב itself is טמא.

steps.title: The verse 'זובו טמא'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'זובו טמא' that זוב is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'His issue is טמא.' This teaches that זוב is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by citing a ברייתא that points to a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'זובו טמא' say outright that the discharge itself is טמא. The next steps show why the ברייתא needed this פסוק at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'His issue is impure' (ויקרא 15:2)
It taught

phrases.english: As it is taught: "His issue is impure"
taught about the זוב that it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'זובו טמא' teaches that זוב is טמא.

steps.title: Why not learn it from a קל וחומר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why a פסוק is needed. Since זוב makes the person טמא, surely it is טמא itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can't we figure this out by logic? It causes טומאה to others, so all the more so it should be טמא itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own need for a פסוק by suggesting a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing זוב makes the man a זב, so it brings טומאה onto someone else. It seems obvious that something which makes others טמא must be טמא itself, so a פסוק looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it a logical deduction?
All the more so (a קל וחומר)
Causes impurity

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical deduction:
it causes impurity to others,
phrases.notes: 'Others' here means the man himself, who becomes a זב because of the discharge.

phrases.english: to itself, is it not all the more so?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the פסוק from step 21 is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'זובו טמא'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר should be enough: what makes others טמא must surely be טמא itself.

steps.title: The שעיר המשתלח breaks the logic
steps.stepSummary: The שעיר המשתלח makes the person who sends it טמא, yet the goat itself is טהור. So the קל וחומר fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: The שעיר המשתלח proves otherwise: it makes others טמא, yet it itself is טהור. So don't be surprised that זוב could also make others טמא and still be טהור itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר by bringing a counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat sent away on יום כיפור makes the one who sends it טמא, but the goat stays טהור. This shows that causing טומאה to others does not prove that a thing is טמא itself, so the logic cannot be relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sent away to עזאזל on יום כיפור
Will prove (a counterexample)
Do not be surprised

phrases.english: The goat that is sent away will prove otherwise,
for it causes impurity to others,
phrases.notes: The one who sends the goat away becomes טמא.

phrases.english: and it itself is pure.

phrases.aramaic: אַף אַתָּה אַל תִּתְמַהּ עַל זֶה,
phrases.english: So you too, do not be surprised about this one,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגּוֹרֵם טוּמְאָה לַאֲחֵרִים
phrases.english: that even though it causes impurity to others
it itself is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proposed in step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The logical deduction that זוב is טמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Something can make others טמא while staying טהור itself, as the שעיר המשתלח shows.

steps.title: So the verse is needed: זוב is impure
steps.stepSummary: Since logic cannot prove it, the פסוק 'זובו טמא' is needed to teach that זוב is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why the פסוק says 'His issue is טמא.' It teaches that זוב is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by repeating the פסוק, now showing why it was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר was knocked down by the שעיר המשתלח, so without a פסוק we might have said זוב is טהור. The פסוק settles that זוב itself is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: זוב is טמא because of the פסוק 'זובו טמא'. A קל וחומר could not prove it, because the שעיר המשתלח makes others טמא while staying טהור itself.

phrases.english: Therefore the verse says: "His issue is impure"
teaching about the זוב that it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the logic is rejected in step 23, the ברייתא shows that the פסוק is needed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'זובו טמא' is the source that זוב is טמא, since logic alone would not prove it.

steps.title: Maybe זוב makes things impure only by touching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: maybe 'זובו טמא' teaches only that זוב is טמא by touching (מגע), not by carrying (משא), like a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: this only applies to touching, but not to carrying, just like a שרץ!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the ברייתא's proof. It suggests the פסוק may be teaching a weaker kind of טומאה: only by touching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא showed that זוב is טמא, but it did not say how strong that טומאה is. There is a real example of something that is טמא by touching but not by carrying: a שרץ. So maybe זוב is like a שרץ, and is טמא only by מגע.

keyTerms.meaning: Touching; making something טמא through physical contact
Carrying; making something טמא by lifting or carrying it, even without touching
A dead creeping animal, one of the sources of טומאה
Just as it is with; used to compare to a known case

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is denying that זוב is טמא. The question is only how far its טומאה reaches: just touching, or carrying too.

phrases.english: But say: these words apply only to touching,
phrases.notes: 'These words' means the ruling learned from 'זובו טמא' a moment ago.

phrases.english: but by carrying, not,
just as it is with a שרץ!
phrases.notes: The point of the comparison: a dead שרץ makes things טמא when you touch it, but not when you carry it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how much the פסוק 'זובו טמא' from step 24 really teaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'זובו טמא' to show that זוב is fully טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק might teach only the weaker level of טומאה (touching only), as we find with a שרץ.

steps.title: No verse is needed for touching
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי answers that we would not need a פסוק to teach that זוב is טמא by touching, since זוב is no less than שכבת זרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: For touching, no פסוק was needed, since זוב is no less than שכבת זרע,
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי starts answering the challenge. He says that touching is already known without the פסוק, and his answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שכבת זרע is טמא by touching. זוב is surely not weaker than שכבת זרע, so we already know זוב is טמא by touching without any פסוק. That means 'זובו טמא' cannot be teaching only touching. It must be teaching something more.

keyTerms.meaning: Semen, which makes things טמא by touching
It is no less (no weaker) than
A פסוק was not needed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the answer to the challenge: if touching is already known, the פסוק 'זובו טמא' must come to teach carrying (משא) as well.

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
For touching, a verse was not needed,
since it is no less than semen,
phrases.notes: The answer isn't finished here. The גמרא continues it on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי: בְּמַגָּע לָא אִיצְטְרִיךְ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by showing that touching is already known without the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the פסוק unnecessary for the smaller point, so it must teach the bigger point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'זובו טמא' might teach only that זוב is טמא by touching, like a שרץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: Touching is already known from שכבת זרע, so the פסוק must teach more than touching. The answer continues on the next amud.
